title: Maps detected by completion and a comparison with power-torsion kernel
statement: Let X be Noetherian, K a quasi-coherent ideal, P,Q,R coherent O_X-modules [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and b:Q -> R. Assume K^t ker(b)=0 for some t >= 1. If f,g:P -> Q satisfy b composed with f = b composed with g and their canonical K-completions are equal as morphisms in Coh(X,K), then f=g. No cokernel bound for b is assumed.

proof.text: On an affine open, d=f-g factors through the finite module T=ker(b). Equality of completions and injectivity of the completed inclusion T -> Q show that the completed map P -> T vanishes.
As K^t T=0, T/K^eT=T once e>=t; the completion of T is naturally T. Hence d=0 on every affine open.
A sheaf morphism is determined on an affine basis: restrict sections to affine neighbourhoods and use separation of the target sheaf. Thus f=g globally.

proof_origin.note: Source argument expanded into an explicit sheaf interface; no new mathematical assumption.

theorem coherentMap_torsion_completion_ext
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (P Q R : CoherentModules X) (b : Q ⟶ R)
    (hker : ∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2
        (kernel b.hom)))
    (f g : P ⟶ Q) (hcomp : f ≫ b = g ≫ b)
    (hcompletion : (completion X K).map f = (completion X K).map g) : f = g
